body.target_estimand: \(D_B(\Sigma_q)=\bar D(B\Sigma_qB^{\top})\), for a supplied rank-\(k\) compression with \(k\leq3\)
body.estimand_functional: For an accepted compressed flag denominator under the stated Gaussian sampling law, \(D_B(\widehat\Sigma_q)/D_B(\Sigma_q)\stackrel{d}{=}\prod_{j=1}^{k}(\chi^2_{n-j+1}/n)^{m_j}=W_m\), where \(m_j=0\) for \(j>k\).

sampling_model.design: Known-zero-mean Gaussian covariance sampling with \(n\widehat\Sigma\sim\mathcal W_3(n,\Sigma)\).
sampling_model.units: The observations \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) are independent vectors in \(\mathbb R^3\); Tamano's Example 2 and the reduced form in equation (22) instantiate them as \((A,M,Y)\), with \(A\) denoting the paper's treatment \(X\), only for the cited three-node front-door benchmark.
sampling_model.treatment: The audit takes any upstream-valid primitive coprime rational causal certificate as input. The Gaussian reduced form \(M=\alpha A+\varepsilon_M\), \(Y=\beta M+\gamma A+\varepsilon_Y\), with \(A,\varepsilon_M,\varepsilon_Y\) mutually independent and nondegenerate, is retained solely as Tamano's equation (22) reduced form in the Example 2 benchmark. In the underlying front-door causal model, \(\gamma\) records association induced by unobserved \(A\)--\(Y\) confounding, not a direct causal effect; the identified total effect is \(\alpha\beta\).
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition enters the algebraic theorem; the sampling parameter is restricted directly to \(\Sigma\in C3\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The classification and rational recognizer are exact algebraic operations. Sampling is used only for Tamano's inherited pivot and confidence set for \(D(\Sigma)\); no inference for \(N(\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\) is asserted.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 proves all-dimensional flag-power sufficiency, ambient-compression invariance, and the exact Gaussian pivot; Theorem 3 and Remark 4 reduce the unrestricted \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) mixed branch to constancy of its kernel line, while the published all-dimensional converse does not derive a flag from self-normalization.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The compressed \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) classification, canonical rank-at-most-three recognition certificate, arbitrary-ambient denominator audit, and all-dimensional corank-one rigidity theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Vanishing of a coordinate-Hessian determinant need not force a hypersurface to be a cone in the relevant ambient dimensions.
Low-dimensional cubic hypersurfaces with vanishing coordinate Hessian include noncone geometries.
A polynomial direction field satisfying its Jacobian-annihilation condition generates an exact quasi-translation.
The half-trek criterion establishes generic identifiability and yields rational recovery in linear structural equation models.
Computer algebra can certify identification of causal effects in polynomially parametrized models.
Fraction-free elimination performs exact determinant and linear-system calculations over integral domains.
Generalized power functions on symmetric cones are products of powers of principal minors relative to a supplied Jordan frame.
Homogeneous matrix cones admit recursive triangular structures induced by cone automorphisms.

body.tldr: The field-tier contribution remains a complete denominator audit for primitive coprime reduced rational causal certificates supported on three covariance variables. The rigidity mechanism is now proved in every matrix dimension on the corank-one branch: adjugate translation needs no homogeneity, and homogeneity plus positive-gradient cone order forces a fixed global kernel line and compression whenever the gradient has rank \(d-1\) somewhere in the positive-definite cone. This closes Tamano's mixed \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) branch without degree or nonresonance restrictions and isolates the higher-dimensional open problem to generic rank at most \(d-2\), where the adjugate vanishes. The resulting \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) classification and terminating rational recognizer decide exactly when a reduced half-trek or related certificate has one nested flag denominator; no full higher-dimensional converse or new coverage theorem is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Tamano leaves the arbitrary-degree mixed rank-two kernel line unresolved in \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\), and the all-dimensional converse assumes rather than derives a common invariant flag. The corank-one kernel obstruction can in fact be removed in every dimension, while the higher-corank branch remains open.
project_justification.niche: The operative algebraic condition is determinant singularity of the trace-pairing symmetric-gradient matrix. Hessian symmetry turns its adjugate into an exact polynomial translation direction in every dimension; positive-cone order then globalizes a corank-one null direction. Coordinate-Hessian geometry and homogeneous-cone automorphisms concern different matrices or stronger supplied structure.
project_justification.fill: The dimension-free rigidity theorem proves a fixed kernel line and compression for every positive-gradient corank-one branch. Its \(d=3\) specialization closes Tamano's remaining mixed branch, completes the nested-flag classification, and makes exact rational recognition and denominator-only Wishart pivot auditing exhaustive for qualifying three-direction primitive reduced rational certificates.

body.related_work: Tamano's Theorem 1 \cite{Tamano2026SelfNormalizing} proves all-dimensional flag-power sufficiency and the exact flag-power Wishart pivot. Theorem 3 proves the three-variable reduction, including determinant stripping, spectral reduction, and the pure branches, while Remark 4 isolates constancy of the mixed kernel line as the missing three-dimensional step. The present \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) theorem closes that branch, and the dimension-free extension additionally proves the fixed-kernel conclusion for every positive-gradient corank-one branch; it does not settle higher-corank branches or furnish a full all-dimensional converse. Tamano's Example 2 gives the background three-node front-door benchmark, with the reduced form in equation (22), the covariance functional \[\tau(\Sigma)=\frac{\sigma_{AM}(\sigma_{AA}\sigma_{MY}-\sigma_{AM}\sigma_{AY})}{\sigma_{AA}(\sigma_{AA}\sigma_{MM}-\sigma_{AM}^{2})}\] in equation (23), and the denominator identity \(D=\Delta_1\Delta_2\) and \(c=10\) in equation (24); Theorem 1 yields \(m=(2,1,0)\) and the denominator pivot \(D(\widehat\Sigma)/D(\Sigma)\stackrel{d}{=}(\chi_n^2/n)^2(\chi_{n-1}^2/n)\). In that benchmark, \(\gamma\) is the reduced-form association generated by unobserved treatment--outcome confounding rather than a direct causal effect, and \(\tau=\alpha\beta\) is the total effect. These benchmark identities are cited background, not solve targets or new claims. Foygel--Draisma--Drton \cite{FoygelDraismaDrton2012HalfTrek} supplies the named family of rational linear-Gaussian causal certificates to which the denominator audit applies after primitive cancellation. García-Puente--Spielvogel--Sullivant \cite{GarciaPuenteSpielvogelSullivant2010ComputerAlgebra} motivates exact certificate-producing causal algebra, and Bareiss \cite{Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity} supplies exact elimination operations. De Bondt \cite{DeBondt2017QuasiTranslations} informs only the finite translation mechanism and does not derive the adjugate direction from a symmetric gradient. Ciliberto--Russo--Simis \cite{CilibertoRussoSimis2008Homaloidal} and Gondim--Russo \cite{GondimRusso2015CubicHessian} study coordinate Hessians, not the matrix-valued trace-pairing gradient used here. Faraut--Korányi \cite{FarautKoranyi1994SymmetricCones} contextualize nested determinant powers. Tunçel--Vandenberghe \cite{TuncelVandenberghe2023HomogeneousCones} derive recursive structures from homogeneous-cone automorphisms; this adjacent mechanism does not settle whether self-normalization alone forces a flag in the remaining higher-corank branch.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For \(S_d\), the trace-pairing gradient uses \((G_P)_{ij}=\tfrac12\partial P/\partial x_{ij}\) for \(i<j\). Polynomiality is essential: the smooth homogeneous Schur-complement function \(y+z-(u^2+v^2)/x\) has a positive-semidefinite rank-two gradient with a moving kernel. Positivity is also essential: \(xu+v^2\) has a singular polynomial gradient with a moving kernel but fails self-normalization. In generic corank at least two, every \((d-1)\times(d-1)\) minor and hence the adjugate vanish identically, so the present translation proof supplies no direction; no lower-cofactor replacement is proved.
body.honest_scope: The new results are dimension-free adjugate-translation invariance, all-dimensional positive-gradient corank-one kernel rigidity and compression, its \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) specialization, the explicit signed mixed-residue bridge, the unrestricted \(\operatorname{Sym}_3\) converse, the rational recognizer, and the exhaustive reduced-denominator audit enabled by that converse. Tamano's flag sufficiency, spectral and determinant reductions, Wishart pivot, and front-door benchmark are cited background. The all-dimensional theorem removes only the corank-one kernel obstruction; it does not prove a complete invariant flag in the generic-rank-at-most-\(d-2\) branch and is not a full higher-dimensional converse. No exact interval, boundary-valid interval, efficiency statement, or coverage theorem for \(\tau\) follows without joint analysis of the numerator and its dependence on the denominator. No software integration, bit-complexity bound, or non-Gaussian inference is claimed.
